title: Honeywell Q3 Earnings: Adjusted EPS Jumps 34% to $2.27 as Margins Expand; 2026 Outlook Raised
excerpt: Sales of $5.0 billion grew 7% organically in the first full quarter after the Aerospace spin-off; segment profit rose 23% and backlog reached nearly $19 billion.
body:
• Honeywell Technologies' third-quarter adjusted EPS rose 34% year over year to $2.27, beating the $2.17 consensus, as sales grew 1% reported and 7% organically to $5.0 billion.
  • Operating margin expanded 640 basis points to 14.8% and segment profit rose 23% to $1.06 billion on productivity, pricing and the elimination of stranded costs from prior spin-offs.
  • Reported EPS fell 20% to $2.40 from continuing operations because the year-ago quarter carried a one-time gain from the Resideo termination agreement.
  • Honeywell raised its full-year 2026 outlook: organic sales growth of 4–5%, adjusted EPS of $8.40–$8.45 and free cash flow of about $2.1 billion.

Honeywell Technologies beat earnings expectations for the third quarter on Thursday and raised its full-year outlook, as the industrial company — reshaped this year by the spin-off of its aerospace business — delivered broad margin expansion across its three remaining segments. It was the first full quarter reported under the new structure, and management used it to argue that the smaller, automation-focused company is also the faster-growing one.

Sales for the quarter ended September 30 rose 1% as reported to $5.0 billion, essentially matching the $5.01 billion consensus estimate compiled by Zacks, but grew 7% on an organic basis as pricing actions and demand across end markets offset the revenue lost to divestitures. Adjusted earnings per share increased 34% year over year to $2.27, ahead of the $2.17 consensus. Operating income jumped 79% to $740 million, with operating margin expanding 640 basis points to 14.8%; segment profit rose 23% to $1.06 billion and segment margin widened 370 basis points to 21.3%, led by Industrial Automation and Building Automation. Reported EPS from continuing operations fell 20% to $2.40, a decline the company attributed primarily to a one-time gain from the Resideo termination agreement recorded in the prior-year quarter. Backlog grew 7% to nearly $19 billion, excluding the divested Warehouse and Workflow Solutions and Productivity Solutions and Services businesses.

Automation Demand Does the Work

Building Automation was the steadiest performer: sales rose about 8% to $2.02 billion, in line with estimates, for an eighth consecutive quarter of growth, with segment profit of $546 million. Process Automation and Technology sales were $1.86 billion, matching estimates, with segment profit of $412 million; management pointed to a multiyear growth inflection in the segment, backed by backlog growth above 10% and strong demand across liquefied natural gas, refining, petrochemicals and low-carbon energy projects. Industrial Automation sales fell sharply on a reported basis to $1.12 billion because of the warehouse and productivity divestitures, but grew about 4% organically. Data-center orders more than doubled in the quarter, with opportunities expanding across building controls, process automation, sensing and liquid cooling.

Cash Flow and the Raised Outlook

Free cash flow rose 15% to $688 million with 95% conversion, even as operating cash flow fell 74% to $607 million against a prior-year quarter flattered by the one-time Resideo settlement; management expects conversion above 100% in the fourth quarter and is targeting gross debt below $13 billion by year-end. For the full year, Honeywell raised its guidance to organic sales growth of 4–5%, adjusted EPS of $8.40–$8.45, free cash flow of about $2.1 billion and total sales of $20.0–20.1 billion, with fourth-quarter organic growth expected at 5–6%. The quarter also closed out a busy portfolio year: the Aerospace spin-off is complete, the company has moved to three reportable segments, it retained a 48% stake in quantum-computing company Quantinuum after its IPO, and it acquired Johnson Matthey's Catalyst Technologies business — while cautioning that supply-chain and geopolitical volatility could still materially affect results.
